newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares edge higher to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares edge higher to new record.

text.p: Turkish shares edged higher in mixed trade on Thursday despite selling prompted by Moody's announcement that it placed under review Turkey's ratings for possible downgrade, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at this year's sixth consequtive all-time high of 1,146, up two points, or 0.17 percent from Wednesday's previous record of 1,044. In dollar terms, it was unchnaged from yesterday's record of $1.04.
Gains totalled 17.4 percent since the market reopened on January 2 after a five-day New Year holiday.
Trade volume jumped to 34.40 trillion lira from Wednesday's 27.34 trillion and neared a record of 35.77 trillion lira recorded on November 29, 1996.
Brokers said profit-taking after recent sharp gains pulled the index down to a low of 1,122 in early trade, but the market later resumed its uptrend.
The index brushed a high of 1,160 in the afternoon, followed by a bout of late selling triggered by the Moody's announcement. The index fell to 1,135 before rebounding again at close.
"The Moody's news was used as an excuse for more profit-taking although it was an expected development," said Alp Tekince from Bumerang securities.

Moody's said in a statement it put Turkey's Ba3 long-term foreign currency sovereign ceiling for bonds on review for possible downgrade, as well as the B1 foreign currency sovereign ceiling for bank deposits.
Lower money and bond market rates, subdued currency trade and 1996 profit prospects were the major reasons buoying the stock market's uptrend since the beginning of 1997.

Of the 234 shares traded, 104 declined, 80 advanced and 50 were unchanged. The IMKB Industrial firmed 0.85 percent to 1,190, the IMKB Services eased 0.49 percent to 1,216, the IMKB Finacial lost 0.81 percent to 1,104.

Actives were led by largely state-owned flat steel giant Eregli, down 250 lira at 14,250, T.Isbank's C series shares, steady at 23,500 lira, utility Cukurova Elektrik, up 2,500 lira at 147,500 and state petroleum refiner Tupras, up 2,000 lira at 32,500. Together, they made up 28.2 percent of the total volume.
